Critique (R2) of S2.1 by security-reviewer, scoped to the owner's threat model (design 18.0, L-GF-39). Targets: the runner GF-RUN-2 (18.4: lib/greenfield/runner.js, run-check.js, serve-check.js, through the frozen lib/evidence.js) and owner acceptance GF-CLOSE-6 (18.5: closure.accept, eccode-gf close accept, events.js, projection). I read 18.0, 18.1, 18.3, 18.4, 18.5, 18.7, the limits register, the code and both test files. I ran tests/gf-runner-copy.test.js and tests/gf-accept.test.js on my copy (34 pass), then wrote reproductions as node tests that assert what the design claims. Every reproduction fails on this tree.

WHAT HELD (gf_run itself). A relative write lands in the copy and is discarded. Discarded writes include another group's file, a new file in another group's area, writes through a relative symlink, writes into a .git or .eccode of the copy, and git commit, exclude entries and assume-unchanged flags made in the copy. The real-tree hash catches absolute writes, absolute symlinks, git -C REAL commits, writes to the real .git/info/exclude and a moved HEAD, and the run fails with the paths named. Copy-back holds as stated: it refuses a real parent that is a symlink, replaces a real symlink or hard-linked file instead of writing through it, and applies deletions first. A role in no group gets nothing back. A temporary directory inside the project fails the run. The repository-naming git variables are removed and GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES stops discovery from the copy. A linked worktree's .git file and its own git dir (inside the common dir) are hashed. GF-CLOSE-6 holds as stated for the cases I tried: only user; a clean tree; not closed or already accepted; every open finding once with its recorded severity, an L-GF-<n> limit and a 30-character reason; no blocking finding; the same checks replayed by the audit; no MCP tool, and the role-locked servers cannot name user.

WHAT BROKE. H2-1 (blocking): the runner is not the only managed-path route for a group role's commands. evidence_run, fix_verify and mutate stay on every role-locked server. They run the plan-pinned commands in the real tree, where a cross-group untracked file and a commit of another group's file pass undetected. The frozen completion check also refuses the runner's evidence as the pinned run, so an agent is steered onto evidence_run. H2-2 (major): .eccode/ is excluded from the real-tree hash on the claim that the record window covers it, but that window covers only three files. Another group's drafts, the evidence logs and the guard configurations can be written through ECCODE_EVIDENCE without detection. H2-3 (minor): GF-CLOSE-6 refuses an empty acceptance list, a condition the documented rule does not state. A non-closable scope with no findings (a readiness no-go that stands) therefore cannot be accepted.

OUTSIDE THE THREAT MODEL (for the limits register):
- Deliberate tampering with git internals or bytes designed to evade the hash: rewriting a .git/objects file (including objects/info/alternates) with the same size, or a change made and restored within one run (L-GF-29).
- Forged events appended outside the hook-covered tools. A forged gf.slice.accepted or gf.slice.closed for a scope makes a later valid acceptance refused, because the "already accepted" and "closed" checks read every such event, valid or not.
- The text-level identity check of the hook. Command forms that hide the acting identity from the text are the named class of 18.3 and L-GF-33. I did not pursue this and record no finding on it. The unbound identity of --actor user (L-GF-17).
- A defeated or disabled hook, or a harness that sends no agent_type.
- No OS isolation (L-GF-40). A process the run starts that leaves its process group (setsid) and writes after the after-snapshot. Writes outside the project.
- Environment fail-open, not reproduced here (git 2.43): gitDirs returns no git directory when git rev-parse --path-format=absolute fails (git older than 2.31), and .git is then not hashed.
- Cache paths (the CACHE pattern) are not compared in the real tree, as 18.4 states.
